children: Gold prices fall to their lowest level in more than three weeks as escalating tensions in the Middle East conflict push energy prices higher, stoking inflation fears and boosting rate-hike bets. In early European trading, New York futures fall 0.5% to $4,372.40 a troy ounce, down 6% on the week. According to CME's FedWatch tool, traders are now pricing in a 70% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in September. Investors now await the release of U.S. economic data, including the August nonfarm payrolls report on Friday. "We expect Friday's payrolls report to determine the next move, as another increase in yields would keep precious metals under pressure, while softer labour data could draw buyers back into the market," analysts at Sucden Financial say. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
